note: Ability handler identification from a controlled 25-second Mos Eisley test: Greedo and Jango stationary, performing a fixed sequence with pauses.

character_id_field.evidence: strb r8, [sb, #0x6BB] at 0x02001D9C in the playable-character constructor 0x02001D20, where r8 is the constructor character-index argument. Values 20 and 29 map onto the ROM-decoded roster as Greedo and Jango Fett, matching who was played.

instance_is_console_not_player: Event counts are exactly symmetric between instances - 457/457, 16483/16483 - because in DS local wireless both consoles simulate both players. Player identity must come from the actor pointer in r0, never from the instance.

ABILITY_B.evidence: Fired only for Jango, sustained 2.6 seconds across one burst, with a 28-unit altitude gain. Sustained hold plus large climb is the jetpack signature; nothing else in the tested sequence is held.

evidence: Fired twice at 2003.1s and 2005.6s in a Jabba match whose only players were IG-88 and Dengar. IG-88 was at speed exactly 0.000 for that entire window, so the move was Dengar s.

Dengar s motion during each burst: a jump to +9.2 and +9.8 above his running plane - the ordinary single-jump height of +9.75 - with horizontal speed rising from a steady 42.0 to 51.3 on the descent. A jump with a forward boost.
He jumped three times in that window but only two produced ABILITY_F, so it is a distinct move rather than a jump side effect.
ABILITY_F.supersedes: The earlier reading of this handler as Greedo s dive specifically. Greedo was the only character it had been seen on; Dengar has it too. The handler covers five controller modes and four action ids, consistent with a family of related moves.

ABILITY_A.evidence: Confirmed by a controlled test where Jango stood completely still: ABILITY_A still fired 84 times for Greedos three jumps. An earlier reading tying it to Jango was wrong.

ABILITY_C.evidence: Fired only on Lando arcs reaching +19.2 units, exactly twice the +9.75 of every single jump measured across Greedo, Jango and Lando. Never fired for any character without a double jump. This also explains an earlier trace recording this address as never executing despite many jumps - no character tested until Lando had one.

ABILITY_E.evidence: Lando arc 3 reached the same +19.15 peak as his double jump but fell in 0.73s against 1.50s - a forced fast descent. ABILITY_E is the only difference between the two arcs.

not_captured: Unholster, fire and holster produced no ability-handler events, so those actions run through routines not in the traced set. Blaster fire is therefore still unlogged.
caveat: Four bursts is a small sample. ABILITY_B is solid; ABILITY_F is plausible; ABILITY_A is not settled.

still_unfired.ABILITY_D: 0x020470D0 - still never fired. Now tested across ten characters AND, in a driven in-match sweep, every one of the twelve buttons plus eighteen combinations including X and Y, which no earlier capture could even record. It is not a button nobody pressed. Next: a write-watchpoint or a call-site search, not more play.

weapons_are_elsewhere: Unholster, fire, holster, Bossks grenade and Boushhs bomb produced no handler events across five characters. Thrown and fired weapons run through routines outside the controller-mode set.

character_run_speed.method: median of per-sample speed over all moving steps in the Jabba match
character_run_speed.spread: Tight - 95th percentile 47.6 for IG-88 and 42.3 for Dengar, so run speed is a per-character constant, not a ramp.

WARNING_r0_is_not_the_actor.finding: On all six ABILITY_* routines r0 points into a pool at 0x0214Exxx-0x0214F1xx, not at the player actor (players were at 0x0212A808, 0x0212B764, 0x02121374).
WARNING_r0_is_not_the_actor.consequence: The field list b0x6bb,0xb0,0xb4,0xb8 is meaningless on these routines - the character index read 0 on every ability row. Abilities must be attributed by motion, or by re-tracing with the actor recovered from another register.
WARNING_r0_is_not_the_actor.also: Addresses in that pool are recycled, so the same r0 value denotes different things at different times.

instances_are_lockstep.finding: Instance 0 and instance 1 produced identical EVENT streams - same actor pointers, same frames, same values, for every ability burst and every player tick.
instances_are_lockstep.consequence: The instance column cannot attribute an ability to a player.
instances_are_lockstep.do_not_delete_inst1: Main RAM is NOT redundant. 63 of the 64 ram.key keyframes differ between the two instances; only the frame-0 keyframe matches. Each DS holds its own local state, so the second RAM capture is real data, not a duplicate. An earlier note here said instance 1 added nothing but volume - that was true of the event stream only and wrong about RAM.

button_mapping_in_arena.evidence: A driven in-match experiment on Boba Fett swept all twelve buttons and eighteen combinations, 45 frames each with 75 idle between, with the other DS held at rest. ABILITY_A fired in every window whose combination contained B - b, r+b, l+b, up+b, a+b - and in no window without it. A, X, Y, R and L alone produced nothing at all.
button_mapping_in_arena.down_plus_B_suppresses_jump: RETRACTED. In the Boba Fett sweep down+b produced no ABILITY_A, but in the Greedo run down+b produced a full jump - peak +9.68. The Boba windows that showed nothing are more likely to be windows where he was airborne or dead than evidence of a suppression rule. Not a decoded behaviour; do not port it.
button_mapping_in_arena.caveat: B = jump is well supported: ABILITY_A fired in every Boba Fett window containing B and none without it, and Greedo jumped on B combinations too. But per-window ability results from Jabba runs must be read against the subject being alive and grounded, which neither driven run guaranteed.

arena_uses_tank_controls.finding: Left and right produce no translation at all - 360-frame holds moved the character zero units - while up and down do. The arena scheme 0x020075EC turns on left/right and translates on up/down.
arena_uses_tank_controls.consequence: The port must not treat left/right as strafing in the arena.

boba_fett_speed_UNRESOLVED.status: RESOLVED - the driven measurement was contaminated, the session figures stand.
boba_fett_speed_UNRESOLVED.what_looked_wrong: A driven experiment measured Boba Fett at 1.18-1.20 u/frame and Greedo at 1.200, about twice every character measured from the recorded sessions.
boba_fett_speed_UNRESOLVED.ruled_out_double_rate: Greedo jumped in the same driven run: peak +9.68 units, airborne 48 frames = 0.80s. Simulating the ROM constants gives +9.69 over 26 ticks, which is 0.87s at 30Hz and 0.43s at 60Hz. The driven run therefore has identical physics at 30Hz - it is not running at double rate, and the earlier 30Hz tick-rate finding is independently confirmed a second time.
boba_fett_speed_UNRESOLVED.actual_cause: The subject was falling, not running. Jabba's Tower is a multi-level tower and a driven character holding a direction walks straight off it. Greedo's movement bursts were y 74.7 -> -61.7 and y 191.4 -> 135.2 - descents, with horizontal motion carried through them. His actor was replaced twice during the experiment, so he died and respawned mid-run, and the four top-speed windows caught him dead: they recorded no motion at all.
boba_fett_speed_UNRESOLVED.conclusion: The session-derived speeds stand and match the motion table at 0x020EE04C exactly. Nothing in the port changes.
boba_fett_speed_UNRESOLVED.lesson_for_experiment_design: Do not measure top speed on Jabba's Tower. A driven character holding a direction reaches an edge in a few seconds and dies. Speed runs need flat, bounded ground - Mos Eisley - or short holds with a verified-constant y and a check that the actor pointer never changes during the window.
